RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the successful candidate are men, making sex discrimination virtually impossible to argue. Raising the panel's gender composition would undermine your credibility, as an all-male panel does not indicate bias against a male applicant in favor of another male applicant. While an all-male panel may reflect poor institutional diversity practices or potential procedural non-compliance with university committee guidelines, it is not evidence of discrimination against you.

The hiring decision likely turned on specific industry experience, departmental fit, or interview performance. Academic administrative processes are notoriously slow, so two weeks without a reply is common. Send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on your interview, but do not raise the panel's gender composition.
